method: Rolling shutters expose the frame one row at a time, so the last row is recorded one full readout later than the first. During a pan the scene moves across the sensor by the pan speed in frame widths per second multiplied by the readout time in seconds, and that travel is the top-to-bottom skew: with a 12.5 ms readout on a 3840 px wide frame and a pan of 0.5 frame widths per second the frame slides 0.5 x 0.0125 = 0.625% of its width, which is 24 px. The edge lean is the arctangent of the skew in pixels divided by the frame height in pixels, so 24 px over 2160 rows is 0.64 degrees from vertical. Row time is the full readout divided by the frame height, and the time to cross one frame width is the reciprocal of the pan speed. Optional vertical motion is multiplied by the readout the same way and reported as a percentage of the frame height, which is the stretch or squash between the first and last row. The tolerance mode inverts the relation: the fastest pan that holds the lean to a chosen percentage of the frame width is the tolerance as a fraction divided by the readout in seconds, so 1% at 12.5 ms is 0.8 frame widths per second, or 1.25 s to cross the frame. Readout time must be between 0.5 ms and 200 ms, frame width and height whole numbers from 64 to 16384 pixels, pan and vertical speeds from 0 to 20 frame widths or heights per second, and the tolerance from 0.01% to 50% of the frame width. A missing, malformed or out-of-range value is rejected with an actionable message rather than defaulted. The model assumes a constant pan and an evenly paced readout: published readout times change with crop, frame rate, binning and codec, and motion blur, uneven row timing, wobble within a frame, lens distortion and stabilisation are not modelled. Calculations run entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Rolling shutter reads the frame row by row, so a pan displaces the last rows against the first by the scene travel during one full readout: skew = frame width x pan speed in frame widths per second x readout time in seconds.
Skew as a fraction of the frame width is pan speed x readout time; the edge lean from vertical is the arctangent of skew pixels divided by frame height pixels.
Vertical motion is stretched or squashed by vertical speed x readout time, and the per-row time is the readout divided by the frame height.
Inverting for a skew tolerance gives the fastest pan as (tolerance / 100) / readout time in seconds, with the crossing time as its reciprocal.
